STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel is a square flat plate. It has a rim band and a flat centre with no inner wall or bowl shadow.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-large, around 26 cm.
b) Reference: the broccoli floret on the right is about 4 cm across, and the plate edge spans roughly 6-7 florets across the width (about 26-28 cm). Taking the plate width as about 26 cm, consistent with cue a).
Final width: 26 cm, area = 676 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Mixed greens (rocket/arugula, raw leafy, mostly under the topping): covers about 25% of the plate (~170 cm²). Average thickness of loose leaves ~2 cm after accounting for the mound. Volume ≈ 170 × 2 = 340 ml × 0.15 = ~50 g.
- Roasted squash/pumpkin pieces (chopped vegetable, ~15% = 100 cm²), mound about 2 cm average (chunky pieces, 3-4 cm peak). Volume ≈ 100 × 2 = 200 ml × 0.6 = ~120 g.
- Broccoli florets (3 pieces, about 4 cm each plus the cluster on the right): roughly 60 g cooked.
- Beef steak (sliced, two-to-three pieces, ~10% area ≈ 65 cm² at ~1 cm average thickness): 65 ml × 1.0 = ~65 g. Grilled steak adds some visible juice/fat, so ~70 g.
- Dressing/oil (thin smear, ~0.3 cm over ~60 cm²): 18 ml × 1.0 = ~15 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: The greens form a base under the squash and broccoli, already counted. No additional hidden layer is evident beyond the plate surface, so no extra items are added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Raw leafy greens (rocket): ~25 kcal
- Roasted squash: ~60 kcal (roasted with oil, ~70)
- Broccoli, cooked: ~35 kcal
- Beef steak, cooked: ~250 kcal
- Dressing/oil: ~400 kcal

Estimated totals: greens 50 g, squash 120 g, broccoli 60 g, beef 70 g, dressing 15 g; total ≈ 315 g.
